issue: The in-figure operator contradicts the caption. The green bar is labelled '>=24.9 GB' (a lower bound) while the caption states compaction 'bounds the footprint across turns at roughly the single-shot level — about 24.9 GB, 27% below the append-only case'. If the value is only known to be >=24.9 GB, it could equal 34.0 GB and the '27% below the append-only case' claim is not established. The bar is also drawn with its right edge exactly at 24.9, so the encoding presents 24.9 as the value while the label presents it as a minimum. The reader cannot tell whether the bar length is the quantity or its floor.
evidence: Figure label: '>=24.9 GB' (green, right of the bar end). Caption: 'compaction (summarize or truncate the accumulated history each turn) bounds the footprint across turns at roughly the single-shot level — about 24.9 GB, 27% below the append-only case'. Independently: 24.9/34.0 = 0.732, i.e. 26.8% below, so the 27% figure is only valid if compaction is approximately 24.9 GB, not merely at least 24.9 GB.
acceptance_test: Make the operator and the encoding agree. Preferred: label the bar '~24.9 GB (bound)' and change the caption to 'bounds the footprint at roughly the single-shot level — about 24.9 GB, i.e. at most ~27% below the append-only case'. If the intent is genuinely a lower bound, label the bar '>=24.9 GB' AND draw it as an open-ended bound (arrow or hatched extension) AND rewrite the caption to remove the '27% below' claim. Verify that no reader can derive '27% below' from a value the figure only bounds from below.

issue: The figure's title promises 'three different things' but the encoding shows one quantity three times, twice identically. All three bars are plotted on a single magnitude axis ('FP16 KV per request (GB)'), and the prefix-cache-eviction bar is drawn to exactly the same length as the append-only bar (34.0 GB). The three things the policies actually move are different quantities — request KV, cached-prefix footprint, and re-prefill cost — and only the first is on the axis. A reader who glances at the chart (or reads only the bar labels) will conclude 'prefix-cache eviction does nothing', which is the opposite of the caption's point that it 'freed cached prefix memory and cost[ing] a re-prefill'.
evidence: Bars: Append-only 34.0 GB (red, dotted); Compaction >=24.9 GB (green, diagonal); Prefix-cache eviction '34.0 GB unchanged' (blue, cross-hatch). Caption: 'prefix-cache eviction leaves the request's own context and KV unchanged (still 34.0 GB) while freeing cached prefix memory and costing a re-prefill.' The in-figure annotation 'evicts the reusable prefix — moves cache/re-prefill' carries the real message in 7-8 pt gray text, below the visual weight of the bars.
acceptance_test: Restructure so the encoding carries the claim: either (a) replace the single-axis bar chart with a small 3-row x 3-column matrix (policy x {request KV, cached-prefix KV, re-prefill tokens}) in which the prefix-cache row differs visibly, or (b) keep the bars but add a second, visually distinct element for the prefix-cache policy showing the re-prefill cost (e.g. a hatched 're-prefill' segment or a callout with the re-prefilled token count), and change the title to match what is plotted. Acceptance: a reader who sees only the figure (no caption) should be able to state that the three policies differ in three different ways.

evidence: Rendered formula block: 'append-only total = I0 + T*6 + T*Y + O_final, T = 4 turns @ 2.62 MB/token (I0 = 9.2K input, 6 = 800 retrieved, Y = 65 generated, O_final = 300 output (once))'. FIGURE 19.2 legend: 'retrieved (6=800)'. Note the sibling symbols I0, Y, O are unambiguous, so the ambiguity is specific to this one glyph.

If it is a digit, replace it with a letter (e.g. R for retrieved) consistently in the FIGURE 19.2 legend, the FIGURE 19.3 formula block, and the FIGURE 19.3 caption/notes, and re-verify that I0 + T*R + T*Y + O_final = 9,200 + 3,200 + 260 + 300 = 12,960 tokens = 34.0 GB. figure: FIGURE 19.2 vs FIGURE 19.3 — cross-figure colour/hatch semantics
issue: The colour+hatch vocabulary is not consistent across two figures two pages apart. In FIGURE 19.2 panel (a): blue diagonal = 'initial context (I0 = 9,200)', green dotted = 'retrieved (6=800)', orange hatch = 'generated (Y=65)', dark green solid = 'output (O=300)'. In FIGURE 19.3: red dotted = 'Append-only', green diagonal = 'Compaction', blue cross-hatch = 'Prefix-cache eviction'. So blue denotes 'initial context' in one figure and 'prefix-cache eviction' in the other, and green denotes 'retrieved' in one and 'compaction' in the other. Red dotted means 'KV/request quantity' in FIGURE 19.2(b) and 'append-only policy' in FIGURE 19.3. The figures are individually defensible (each is directly labelled, and hatch patterns survive grayscale), but the book does not hold one visual language for 'policy' versus 'quantity'.
evidence: FIGURE 19.2 legend swatches: blue diagonal, green dotted, orange hatched, dark green solid. FIGURE 19.3 bars: red dotted, green diagonal, blue cross-hatch. No legend or note in either figure states that the two figures share a colour vocabulary.
acceptance_test: Establish and apply one rule across Ch 19 figures — e.g. reserve a single hue family for policies (FIGURE 19.3) and a different family for token categories (FIGURE 19.2) — or add a one-line note that colours are local to each figure.
